newsitem.title: UK: Euro shares above lows, dollar below highs.
newsitem.headline: Euro shares above lows, dollar below highs.

text.p: Fears of higher interest rates and news of U.S. missile attacks on Iraq rattled Wall Street and European bourses on Tuesday but the markets later fought back, recovering from their lows.
A key U.S. economic indicator which turned out weaker than expected calmed market nerves over the need for higher U.S. rates and took some pressure off stock and bond markets.

The U.S. retaliation for weekend incursions by Iraqi troops into Kurdish areas fired the oil market to post-Gulf War peaks in Asian trading but oil prices later slipped back and went into reverse in late European business.

Gold and the dollar, often safe havens for funds at times of crisis, eased from earlier highs, although the U.S. currency stayed quite buoyant against the yen in view of Japan's dependence on imported oil.

The Dow Jones industrial average of blue-chip stocks lost more than 50 points within 10 minutes of Wall Street's opening, the first time the key New York share market had traded this week and could react to the renewed tensions in the Middle East.

The selloff on Wall Street following Monday's Labor Day holiday was also prompted by mounting fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve might increase interest rates before elections in November to keep inflationary pressures in check.
A report in the Wall Street Journal said U.S. policy makers were considering a larger-than-expected 0.5 percent rise in the key Fed funds interest rate.

Market nerves then steadied after the U.S. NAPM purchasing managers index for August came out at 52.6, less than an expected 52.9 and likely to provide the U.S. central bank with fewer fears about overheating.
The Dow was down around 17 points as European markets closed and later moved into the plus column.
But traders were on alert for even more important news on Friday -- key U.S. August non-farm payrolls data -- for clues on when interest rates are likely to rise.
On London's International Petroleum Exchange, October futures for benchmark Brent crude were down 21 cents at $21.78 a barrel in early evening business.
Brent earlier hit a post-Gulf War high of $23.50 in Asian trading to add to a gain of $1.21 on Monday after the United Nations delayed implementation of an Iraqi oil-for-food deal.
But investors later cashed in some profits in the absence of an escalation of the confrontration.

Gold gained around 60 cents an ounce to $387.50 in early European trade but then turned round to show little net change on the day. Bullion traders remembered losing a lot of money during the 1990 Gulf War when bullion soared and then collapsed.

The dollar also slipped from earlier highs around 109.45 yen and 1.4912 marks, closing lower against the mark and steady against the yen after a brief rise on news of the U.S. military intervention failed to spark follow-through buying.
"For the currency markets, the Iraq story proved to be a bit of a non-event," said Julian Jessop at Nikko Europe.

"The markets seem to feel that this situation is not going to escalate much more," said David Bloom, currency economist at HSBC James Capel. "It has helped boost the dollar initially but the focus is now back on economic data."
A rebound in U.S. stocks and bonds helped the London stock market, Europe's biggest, recover from its lows by the close.

French stocks fell but finished well above their lows as reassuring U.S. economic data offset nervousness triggered by the missile attacks. Brokers said the strength of oil shares, buoyed by higher oil prices, came to the aid of the bourse.
German shares closed in the minus column but revived from their lows in late computerised business.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted around 109.25 yen and 1.4835 marks, compared with 109.14 and 1.4863 in late business on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 28.5 points lower at 3,855.9.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed floor trade 22.11 adrift at 2,510.77 but revived in later computerised business to 2,528.73. In Paris, the CAC-40 share index ended down 5.55 at 1,971.43.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold was fixed at $386.60 an ounce in the afternoon, down from the morning fix of $387.20. It closed London trading around $386.95, virtually unchanged from the previous close. Silver eased one cent to $5.18.
